reasoning:
The claim is entirely accurate. Octopuses possess three hearts and blue blood, which are evolutionary adaptations for survival in their marine environments:
1. **Three Hearts**: An octopus has two branchial hearts and one systemic heart. The two branchial hearts pump deoxygenated blood through the gills to load up on oxygen, while the single systemic heart circulates the oxygenated blood to the rest of the body.
2. **Blue Blood**: Unlike humans and other vertebrates who use iron-based hemoglobin (giving blood a red color), octopuses use a copper-based protein called hemocyanin to transport oxygen. Because hemocyanin contains copper, it turns blue when bound to oxygen (oxygenated blood) and becomes colorless when deoxygenated.
